own_solution.law: Hagen–Poiseuille flow gives Q = πd²v/4, Δp = 32ηLv/d², and P = ΔpQ. With SI inputs, Q = 2.51327412×10⁻⁶ m³/s and Δp = 3200 Pa, giving P = 8.04247719 mW. Adding length q at the stated speed multiplies the power by (L + q)/L.
assumptions: The usual no-slip condition applies at the pipe wall.
The stated average speed applies to the evaluated flow after any preceding pipe extension.
The added pipe continues the stated straight, horizontal, uniform-bore geometry and flow model.

notes: I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag: the claims explicitly identify T0EC4 and T4C1C as numeral-free controls, rather than number-preserving minimal pairs. Their wording matches their named twins with the numerical length replaced by 'short length'. Both explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve 5.1 m and change only the relevant object or timing. For added pipe lengths 3.4, 5.1 and 7.3 m, the calculated powers are respectively 21.7146884, 28.5507940 and 37.3975189 mW, agreeing with every certified answer at its displayed precision. All disconnected and cancelling variants retain 8.04248 mW. Outlet pressure cancels because inlet pressure increases by the same amount at the prescribed flow rate; pressure units must be converted consistently when evaluating the cancellation expression. The pass-1 answers were expressed in W; this pass uses the authors' target unit, mW.
